definition: A relationship $y = kx$ with $k$ constant, so doubling one variable doubles the other; its graph is a straight line through the origin.
A relationship $y = \frac{k}{x}$ with $k$ constant, so doubling one variable halves the other and their product stays the same; its graph is a curve that approaches both axes without touching them.
$R^2$, a value from 0 to 1 showing how well a trend line or curve fits the data; the closer it is to 1, the closer the points lie to the line.
A single straight line or smooth curve drawn through plotted points so that they are scattered as evenly as possible on both sides of it, ignoring anomalous points.
The steepness of a line: the change in the $y$ quantity divided by the change in the $x$ quantity, with units of the $y$ unit per $x$ unit, such as $\pu{cm3 s-1}$ for a rate.
A line drawn through a plotted point, extending by the absolute uncertainty on each side, to show the range in which the true value is likely to lie.
Estimating a value by extending a graph or trend line beyond the range of the measured data; it is less reliable because the trend may not continue.
Estimating a value from a graph or trend line within the range of the measured data.
The variable an experimenter changes on purpose; it is plotted on the horizontal axis.
The variable that is measured to see how it responds to changes in the independent variable; it is plotted on the vertical axis.
